rv.q: That dreamlike quality is spellbindingly realised in the shifting, subtle hues of Peter Mumford’s lighting, and in the precise articulation of its players.
Ian Rickson's production is exquisitely pointed.
It is both a beautifully clear production and one which, through the alternate casting, adds to the bottomless mystery of Pinter's play.
This way round, it has a raw intensity and haunting mystery which the other permutation doesn’t achieve.
One of the theatrical treats of the year would be to see Old Times twice, with each of the casting arrangements.
Rickson’s production charts all these shifting tonal alliances with exquisite good taste...

cn.t: Critics praise Ian Rickson's production of Pinter's *Old Times* as a compelling revival, with Kristin Scott Thomas and Lia Williams delivering powerhouse performances in their alternating roles alongside Rufus Sewell.
